newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. urges Israel to scrap E.Jerusalem housing plan.
newsitem.headline: U.N. urges Israel to scrap E.Jerusalem housing plan.

text.p: The General Assembly, by an overwhelming majority, called on Israel on Thursday to abandon plans to build new Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem.
The resolution was similar to one vetoed by the United States in the Security Council last Friday.
The vote in the Assembly was 130 in favour, with two against and two abstentions.

Arab states, frustrated by last week's U.S. veto, transferred the issue to the 185-nation Assembly, where a day-long debate was held Wednesday. There is no veto in the Assembly, whose decisions are not binding.

As in last week's council session, virtually all speakers in the Assembly criticised Israel's decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a hill between East Jerusalem and Bethlehem that Israel captured during the 1967 Middle East war. The area is called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians.
Israel regards Jerusalem as its undivided capital. The Palestinians regard East Jerusalem as the capital of an eventual Palestinian state.
